summary: Whole field lit at once by a lamp or LED through a filter cube; a camera records it in one exposure. No optical sectioning. Cell culture, slides, thin samples.
status: Experimental. Our own wording of the cited sources; a cause stays 'consistent with' until the alternatives are ruled out. Scope feature lines are unverified until a facility checks them; `seenInFiles` is what the lab's own files record.

stages.does: A lamp or LED lights the whole field through the excitation filter; its intensity setting and the field diaphragm set how much light, and how evenly.

symptoms.symptom: The centre of the field is brighter than the edges, or the same kind of object reads brighter in the middle.
symptoms.explanation: Illumination and collection are not flat across the field (shading, vignetting), so a pixel's value depends on where in the field it sits. Intensities compared across the field, or across fields placed differently, carry that pattern.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: background or objects brighter in the centre than at the corners (look at the image; Cecelia does not measure field flatness yet). A flat-field image of a uniform fluorescent slide shows the pattern itself.
symptoms.alternatives: Thicker tissue or denser cells in the middle of the sample, or a real gradient of the label.

stages.does: A filter cube (excitation filter, dichroic, emission filter) picks which dye is excited and which emission reaches the camera; one cube per channel, imaged one after the other.

symptoms.symptom: The same objects appear in two channels.
symptoms.explanation: A dye's emission or excitation spectrum overlaps the other cube's band (bleed-through, crosstalk), so a bright label shows in a channel it was not meant for.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: the channels' shared structure; a single-label control imaged through both cubes.
symptoms.alternatives: The two labels really are on the same objects (co-localisation), or autofluorescence present in both bands.

stages.does: Collects the light; magnification and NA set resolution, light collected, and with the camera pixel the pixel size.
Fluoresces, bleaches under the light, and in a widefield image contributes light from above and below the focal plane as well as from it.

symptoms.symptom: A diffuse haze around bright objects; dim objects sit on a raised, blurred background.
symptoms.explanation: A widefield microscope collects light from the whole depth of the sample, not only the focal plane, so out-of-focus light adds a blurred background. Thicker samples add more.
symptoms.check: Light path: technology widefield; Acquired data: background level (noise.bgLevel) high relative to objects (photons.objects).
symptoms.alternatives: Diffuse real staining (a label in the cytoplasm or medium), autofluorescence, or a dirty coverslip.

symptoms.symptom: Fields imaged later, or imaged again, are dimmer.
symptoms.explanation: Each exposure, and time spent focusing under the lamp, bleaches the dye. Fields that saw more light read dimmer for the same labelling.
symptoms.check: Acquisition: acquiredAt order of the images against their brightness; exposure and illumination intensity per channel.
symptoms.alternatives: Fewer or weaker-labelled cells in those fields (biology), or a focus that drifted.

stages.does: Records the image: exposure time sets how long light is collected, gain amplifies the read-out, a fixed offset keeps the dark level above zero.

symptoms.symptom: The brightest objects are flat-topped at the top value.
symptoms.explanation: Pixels past the camera's full well or its digitiser's top value (4095 at 12 bit) are clipped; their intensity is lost, and sums or means over them read low.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: clipped % and top value against the camera's bit depth (Acquisition: camera.bitDepth); a 12-bit camera in a 16-bit file tops out at 4095, not 65535.
symptoms.alternatives: None for the clipped pixels themselves; a very bright artefact (debris) can be the clipped object.

symptoms.symptom: Objects barely stand out from a grainy background.
symptoms.explanation: Few photons per pixel: the shot noise of the signal and the camera's read noise are large next to it. Longer exposure or binning collect more per pixel; each costs time, bleaching or resolution.
symptoms.check: Acquisition: exposureMs, gain, camera.binning; Acquired data: noise.snr and photons.objects (Foi-style noise fit).
symptoms.alternatives: Weak or failed labelling (biology or staining), or the wrong filter cube for the dye.

symptoms.symptom: The darkest pixels are well above zero.
symptoms.explanation: A scientific camera adds a fixed offset (dark level) so noise is not cut at zero; background never reaches 0. Subtract the dark level, not the image minimum. A camera has no photon-counted floor: that reading belongs to a photon-counting detector, so a 'photon-counted' floor on a camera channel is a misread, not a finding.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: floor and noise.bgMedian; zero % near 0 is expected on a camera.
symptoms.alternatives: Real background fluorescence (medium, autofluorescence) on top of the offset.

symptoms.symptom: Images of one set that should be comparable differ in brightness.
symptoms.explanation: Exposure, camera gain or illumination intensity changed between images. Raw intensities are only comparable at the same settings; a changed exposure scales the signal, and gain scales signal and noise together.
symptoms.check: Acquisition: exposureMs, gain and illuminationIntensity per channel, compared across the set's images.
symptoms.alternatives: Real differences between samples or conditions, uneven field placement, or bleaching.

stages.does: Turns the camera read-out into numbers: bit depth sets the range, binning adds neighbouring pixels into one.

symptoms.symptom: Small objects (a few hundred nm to ~1 µm) span only one or two pixels.
symptoms.explanation: Binning sums neighbouring pixels: more signal per pixel, coarser pixels. Resolving a feature needs a pixel about half its size or smaller (Nyquist); counting bright spots needs less than measuring their size or shape.
symptoms.check: Acquisition: camera.binning, camera.sensorPixelUm and objective magnification; Image: pixel size against the size of the objects in question.
symptoms.alternatives: Coarse is normal when the question is a count or a presence, not a size; ask what the images are for before calling it a mistake.

stages.does: Repeats the exposure over z positions or time points, or tiles fields.
